disagreements.topic: How much of revenue is Technology & Load Centers (data centers)
disagreements.positions: agent_3 (round 2): ~10% of 2025 revenue, so ~24% of 2026E revenue. agents 1, 2, 4 and 5 took the round-1 supervisor's '~10% of 2026 revenue' and used it to soften their bear cases.
disagreements.resolution: agent_3 is right, and the round-1 supervisor misread the table. The ~10% column is labelled '% of 2025 Quanta Revenue', and the segment is guided to grow 220-240% in 2026, partly from acquisitions (Dynamic Systems, Tri-City, Phalcon). Weighting the table's growth rates implies 2025 revenue of ~$28.6B against the $39.5B 2026 guide. That puts Technology & Load Centers at ~$9.1-9.7B, or ~23-25% of 2026 revenue. Direct data-center exposure is roughly 2.4x what four agents assumed. So the Texas permit halt, other state moratoria and any hyperscaler digestion hit 2027 guidance more directly, and PWR is more correlated with AI-capex names.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 2026 Operational and Financial Commentary, Supplemental Disclosure table (p.10): columns '% of 2025 Quanta Revenue' and '2026E Revenue Growth'. Technology & Load Centers ~10% / 220-240%. Utility ~50% / 20-25%. Generation ~25% / 10-15%. 2026 revenue guide midpoint $39.5B.

disagreements.positions: agent_5 cut its bear weight from 22% to 20%, citing Kalshi 2027 recession at 21% ($538k volume) and ~10% data-center exposure. agents 1, 2 and 4 hold the bear at 22%, agent_3 at 25%.
disagreements.resolution: The Kalshi figure checks out: KXRECSSNBER-27 last traded at $0.21 (bid 0.20 / ask 0.21), volume ~$538k. The market resolves on two consecutive negative GDP quarters from Q4 2026 to Q4 2027, a narrower test than NBER. That is a deep market and a fair replacement for the thin Polymarket one. The other half of agent_5's reason, ~10% data-center exposure, is wrong (it is ~24%). Net, the agents' 20-22% bear weight is not too heavy, and the agents that softened bear EPS for low AI exposure were slightly too generous in the $400-600 zone.
disagreements.evidence: Kalshi public API, market KXRECSSNBER-27 (fetched 2026-10-02); Q2 ops commentary table.

disagreements.positions: All five agents cite '+17.3% on Q2-26 and about -2.5% after Q3-25' as evidence that reactions run both ways.
disagreements.resolution: The -2.5% is not in the daily closes. Close to close, the Q3-25 print day (Oct 30, 2025) was +1.1% ($448.69 to $453.83) and the next day -1.0%. The three 2026 prints were all up: Q4-25 on Feb 19 +6.7% ($519.31 to $554.00), Q1-26 on Apr 30 +15.8% ($628.60 to $727.77), and Q2-26 on Jul 30 +17.3%. The claim started in agent_5's round-1 file and spread through the round-1 supervisor. Reactions have been large, but over the last four prints they were not two-sided. Consensus has since risen sharply (Q3 $4.99, 19 up / 0 down revisions in 30 days), so the bar is higher. That justifies only a small upward tilt in the 1-month ladder.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data daily closes Sep 30, 2025 to Oct 1, 2026; EDGAR 8-K (Item 2.02) filing times Oct 30 2025, Feb 19, Apr 30 and Jul 30 2026, all before the open; Alpha Vantage earnings estimates.

disagreements.topic: Fair value ($630-677) and where the multiple settles
disagreements.positions: agent_3 $630 (keeps a 1.5% EPS haircut, 19x EBITDA, adds a 3% FCF yield on 2027 FCF). agent_4 $677 (2028 FCF at 3%). Others $655-671. All now use ~30-30.5x Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$21.6-22.4 after the Sep 16 hike.
disagreements.resolution: The spread now comes mostly from method weights, not facts. agent_3's small haircut is defensible once data centers are ~24% of revenue and Texas has halted all data-center permits. But FY27 consensus keeps rising ($19.64 to $19.77 over 30 days, 24 up / 0 down), which argues against a larger cut. Reconciled fair value is ~$660, near the five-agent mean of $658 and spot. That is down from the round-1 supervisor's $668 because every agent now takes about a turn off the multiple for the Fed hike.
disagreements.evidence: Alpha Vantage EARNINGS_ESTIMATES (FY27 $19.77, 26 analysts, range $17.48-22.02); CNBC Sep 16 FOMC; agent method tables.

disagreements.positions: agents 1-2: P(>=1160) ~0.09, P(>=1325) ~0.05. agents 4-5: ~0.034 / ~0.01. agent_3: 0.059 / 0.027. Bull prices are similar ($920-940); the difference is in tail shape.
disagreements.resolution: Search cannot settle this. A +75% year would need ~38x on ~$26 NTM EPS. That is above both the bull cases and the ~35x at which the stock trades now while the Fed is hiking. But PWR rose +57% in the last 12 months ($420.65 to $662.60), so the fat tail is not implausible. I leave it at the mean.

Keep $455 (~23x FY27 consensus of $19.77). agent_3's higher data-center share argues that a fundamental break would show up sooner, i.e. a higher level. agent_1's and agent_5's point that a rates-only de-rating would stop at ~$470-600 argues for a lower one. $455 sits in the middle and above the $404.51 52-week low (Oct 22, 2025).
disagreements.evidence: Agent files; Alpha Vantage FY27 consensus; Twelve Data low $404.51 intraday Oct 22, 2025.

disagreements.positions: All agents: Q3 print ~Oct 29 (unconfirmed, ~85-90% inside the window), FOMC Oct 27-28. agents 2 and 3 add the TCEQ compliance update due Oct 19.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed. As of 2026-10-02 the IR calendar still shows 'no upcoming events', and the only 8-K since Aug 6 is the Sep 15 board appointment (Item 5.02/7.01, Ellen Rubin), which is immaterial. The Texas governor's Sep 21 directive requires TCEQ to report on compliance by Monday Oct 19, 2026, and halts all state approvals for data centers until the ERCOT/TWDB audits are done.
disagreements.evidence: Quanta IR calendar; EDGAR 8-K list (Sep 15, 2026 Ex. 99.1); gov.texas.gov release Sep 21, 2026.

one_month_reasoning: The Q3 print (~Oct 29, unconfirmed, ~85-90% inside the window), FOMC Oct 27-28 and the TCEQ update Oct 19 all fall in the window. Over the last four prints, reactions were +1.1%, +6.7%, +15.8% and +17.3% (not '-2.5%'). Against that, consensus has been revised up hard to $4.99. So I tilt only slightly up from the forecasters' mean (P(>= $662.60) 0.517 vs 0.503) and keep a ~13% one-month sigma.
confidence_reason: My checks settled one disagreement that matters: data centers are ~24% of 2026 revenue, not ~10%. Four agents used the wrong figure to soften their bear cases, so I shade P(close >= K) down 0.4-1.0 points for K = $398-663. I also corrected the earnings-reaction base rate. The effect on the 12-month distribution is small and partly offset by the verified 21% Kalshi recession odds and rising FY27 estimates, so this does not reach 'high'.
thesis_break_reason: $455 is ~23x FY27 consensus EPS of $19.77, the peer and pre-2023 multiple, ~31% below spot and above the $404.51 52-week low. A rates-only de-rating to ~26-28x would stop around $515-555. Reaching $455 would take a real break: a 2027 guide below consensus, a sequential backlog decline, NiSource or large-load programs slipping out of 2027, or a hyperscaler or state-permitting retrenchment. That last one matters more now that Technology & Load Centers is ~24% of revenue.
key_drivers: Record backlog of $53.4B, +49% YoY, with 12-month backlog of $32.3B (+61%). Most of the NiSource program is still excluded (Q2 8-K, ops commentary).

Valuation: ~33.5x FY27 consensus of $19.77, rising with 24 up / 0 down revisions in 30 days. Agents assume ~30x on Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$22 after the Sep 16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00%, so the price outcome turns more on the multiple than on EPS.

Direct data-center exposure is ~24% of 2026 revenue (corrected from ~10%). The Texas halt on all state data-center approvals (TCEQ report due Oct 19) and any 2027 hyperscaler digestion feed into guidance directly.
Q3 print ~Oct 29 against a raised $4.99 consensus. The last three prints rallied 7-17% on the day.
Macro: Kalshi prices a 2027 technical recession at 21% (deep market), and the Fed signals one more 2026 hike.

fair_value.reason: ~30x Oct-2027 NTM adj EPS of ~$22 (25% FY27 $19.77 + 75% FY28 ~$22.9-23.3) and ~19.5-20x NTM EBITDA of ~$5.3B, less ~$5.9B net debt, over ~152.5M diluted shares, give ~$650-680. A small allowance for the larger data-center share (~24% of revenue) under the Texas permit halt brings it to ~$660, about spot and in line with the five-agent mean of $658. The round-1 figure of $668 used a ~31x multiple, before agents took a turn off for the Sep 16 hike.

summary: In round 2 the five forecasts converged (fair values $630-677, mean $658, P(>= $663) ~0.52). Each now assumes ~30x Oct-2027 NTM EPS after the Sep 16 Fed hike, so EPS growth of ~16-18% roughly offsets de-rating. The main fact correction is that data centers are ~24% of 2026 revenue, not ~10%: agent_3 caught the round-1 misread. Four agents used the wrong figure to soften their bear cases, so I shade the $400-660 zone down by up to a point. I also found that the widely repeated '-2.5% after Q3-25' reaction is not in the price data (it was +1.1%; 2026 prints were all +7-17%), which earns a slight upward tilt into the ~Oct 29 print. Fair value is ~$660, thesis break $455, and the edge over the index is small.

sizing.entry: 2 tranches: half after the Q3 print (~Oct 29) and the Oct 27-28 FOMC, half over the following 4-6 weeks
sizing.overlap: VST (AI and data-center power demand), GOOGL and AVGO (hyperscaler AI capex). With data centers ~24% of PWR revenue, the overlap is bigger than the round-1 figure implied; together these are ~14% of the portfolio.
sizing.reason: PWR is a high-quality operator with record backlog. But at ~33.5x FY27 EPS with ~44% realized volatility and fair value near spot, it is unlikely to beat SPY's Sharpe ratio. The corrected ~24% data-center share deepens its overlap with the existing AI-capex and power cluster (VST, GOOGL, AVGO), and an earnings print plus an FOMC meeting land in four weeks. So I cap it at 4%, below round 1's 5%, and scale in after the events.
